official.deadline_note: Sciences Po has not published a fixed calendar date for the scholarship's own deadline. What is published: the application-fee-waiver request window runs from October to mid-December 2026, and the programme page states that detailed information and the application timeline for the waiver will be published there. The linked admissions deadlines page states that applicants for the Boutmy or Mastercard scholarship must submit before the scholarship deadline 'regardless of the deadline of the requested programme(s)', with the general closing date for two-year Master's programmes being 21 February 2027 (11.59pm, Paris time) and 3 January 2027 for the Joint Master in Journalism and International Affairs and the Master in Journalism.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake (admissions for the 2027 intake are open; fee-waiver window October to mid-December 2026)
official.status_note: The Mastercard Foundation's own partner page lists Sciences Po admissions as 'Open', and the Sciences Po graduate page states 'Admissions for the 2027 intake are open'. The graduate-study page states that applications for the fee waiver will be open from October to mid-December 2026 and that detailed information and the application timeline will be published on that page.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Sciences Po states: 'Scholarships cover the full cost of tuition and living expenses in France, throughout the recipient's time studying at Sciences Po.'
benefits: The Program covers the full financial needs of selected Scholars and provides comprehensive support throughout their two years of study at Sciences Po

eligibility: Hold the citizenship of an African country; applicants holding dual citizenship that includes citizenship of a country outside the African continent are not eligible
Be currently completing, or already hold, a Bachelor's degree from one of the universities on the published list of partner institutions
Or be currently completing or hold a Bachelor's degree and have participated in a recognised bridge programme or mentoring programme offered by one of the approved organisations
Or be currently completing or hold a Bachelor's degree and currently hold, or have previously held, UNHCR refugee status
Be under 35 years of age on 1 September of the year in which the scholarship application is submitted
Not already hold, or currently be pursuing, a Master's degree; be applying to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for the first time
Meet Sciences Po's academic requirements, including the mandatory table of minimum academic results required according to the country of the home university
Apply to and be admitted to a two-year Master's programme at Sciences Po (dual degree programmes and one-year Master's programmes are not eligible)
Not currently enrolled at Sciences Po, and not currently enrolled in or graduated from a French higher education institution
requirements: Demonstrate a clear alignment between the chosen Master's programme at Sciences Po, personal and academic background, and future career goals
Demonstrate critical thinking and analytical insight into the major contemporary political, economic and societal challenges facing Africa and the world
Demonstrate ambition, originality and perseverance through entrepreneurial initiatives or public service projects with potential to contribute to Africa's socio-economic transformation
Submit a complete application; any missing or non-compliant supporting document renders the application incomplete and therefore ineligible
Consult the mandatory table of minimum academic results before applying; applicants below the threshold are automatically deemed ineligible
Be selected by the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program Selection Committee
documents: Valid identity document (passport, national identity card, or travel document)
Proof of completion or current completion of a Bachelor's degree (transcript, diploma or certificate) at one of the recognised partner universities
Or proof of a Bachelor's degree plus a certificate confirming successful completion of a recognised bridge programme
Or proof of a Bachelor's degree plus proof of refugee status (UNHCR registration card)
Academic recommendations, which must not be submitted from a personal email address
Language test results as required by the chosen Master's programme
Written scholarship application responses and interview
selection_criteria: Having faced significant barriers to accessing education, whether economic, social, geographical, or resulting from other circumstances

Demonstrating a strong commitment to advancing the development of the African continent and a clear aspiration to become a changemaker, particularly in the fields of public policy and political, environmental and societal transitions

Demonstrating strong potential for transformative leadership, together with the capacity and determination to create a positive, sustainable and measurable impact within one's community, country, or across the African continent
Particular consideration is given throughout the selection process to applications from young women, refugees and displaced persons, and persons with disabilities

Verify eligibility for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

official.application_route: Single online application through the Sciences Po application platform (admission.sciencespo.fr) via the International Graduate Admissions Procedure: request the fee waiver, then apply to a two-year Master's programme in the same file.
official.study_mode: Full-time, in person in Paris (all Master's programmes are in person for a duration of two years, ten months per year)
official.citizenship_residency: Must hold the citizenship of an African country; applicants holding dual citizenship that includes citizenship of a country outside the African continent are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The Program is designed for students from the African continent and is only accessible through the international graduate admissions procedure, which is open to applicants holding a non-French undergraduate degree (or 180 ECTS) from an institution in France or abroad. Students currently enrolled in, or graduated from, a French higher education institution are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must apply to a two-year Master's programme at Sciences Po through the International Graduate Admissions Procedure; dual degree programmes and one-year Master's programmes are not eligible, and the undergraduate degree must come from a listed partner institution or an approved bridge/mentoring programme, or the applicant must hold or have held UNHCR refugee status
official.duration: Two years of Master's study, in person in Paris (ten months per year)
official.description: Sciences Po describes the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program as designed for students from the African continent who wish to pursue a two-year Master's degree at Sciences Po, covering the full financial needs of selected Scholars and providing comprehensive support throughout their two years of study. The scholarship is comprehensive: it covers the full cost of tuition and living expenses in France throughout the recipient's time at Sciences Po, and support runs from the moment candidates are selected until they secure their first job. Sciences Po is the only institution from the European Union and the only francophone university outside the African continent to partner with the Mastercard Foundation.
official.region: Africa (scholars); studies take place in Paris, France
official.program_type: Fully funded graduate scholarship for a two-year Master's degree
official.english_requirement: Sciences Po states there is no language requirement to apply to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, which welcomes students from both francophone and anglophone countries. However, applicants must meet the language requirement of the Master's programme they apply to: where required, test results must be attached directly in the online application by the deadline, and although some programmes require no specific English level for admission, a C1 English level must be proven by the end of the two years in order to obtain the Master's degree. For the 2027 intake, language tests must have been taken on 1 January 2025 or later, and exemptions apply for applicants who studied at least two consecutive years in a degree programme fully taught in English.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a needs-plus-merit award, not a fixed stipend: Sciences Po covers your tuition and living expenses in full for both years but never publishes a monthly figure, so budget against Paris living costs without assuming a specific allowance. Your application file does double duty, because the same Sciences Po platform submission carries both the Master's admission request and the fee-waiver request that puts you into the Mastercard running. The single hardest gate is institutional, not academic: if your Bachelor's does not come from a listed partner university or an approved bridge programme, and you do not hold or have held UNHCR refugee status, you cannot enter the programme at all.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An under-35 African citizen who completed a Bachelor's at a listed partner university (or an approved bridge programme, or holds UNHCR status), has never held or studied for a Master's, and wants a two-year Master's in Paris with no tuition or living-cost exposure.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your undergraduate institution appears on the Sciences Po partner-institution PDF, or that your bridge/mentoring programme is on the approved list, before anything else
Check your country's row in the mandatory minimum academic results table, since falling below it is an automatic rejection rather than a discretionary one
Build one complete application file that satisfies both the Master's admissions requirements and the Mastercard document list, and treat missing items as fatal
Secure academic referees early and insist they submit from institutional email addresses, because personal-address recommendations are explicitly flagged as non-compliant
Book any required language test in time to hold the result by your deadline; for the 2027 intake the test must be dated on or after 1 January 2025
Watch the programme page and the programme's LinkedIn and Instagram accounts for the fee-waiver window and the scholarship's own deadline, which Sciences Po had not published as of 10 October 2026
common_rejection_risks: Applying a second time: a previous unsuccessful Mastercard application permanently bars you from applying again, and the rule is enforced strictly
Dual citizenship that includes any non-African country, which makes you ineligible regardless of your academic record
Choosing a dual degree or a one-year Master's, both of which are excluded and cannot be rescued by a strong file
Prior or current enrolment at Sciences Po or any French higher education institution, including graduates of French institutions
An incomplete file, missing transcripts or language results, or a recommendation sent from a personal email address, all of which make the application ineligible rather than merely weak
Missing the country-specific minimum academic result threshold, which triggers automatic ineligibility before any holistic review
AI-assisted written answers, which Sciences Po warns may result in a lower evaluation because they produce standardised responses
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Sciences Po publishes no monthly stipend figure, so the value of the living-cost coverage cannot be quantified from official pages. The scholarship is awarded only to the Scholar and explicitly cannot be extended to family members or dependents, so any accompanying family's housing, schooling and healthcare in Paris remain entirely out of pocket. Because Sciences Po covers 'full financial needs', there is no published list of applicant-borne costs, but candidates who are admitted without the award must fund the non-EEA graduate tuition of EUR 20,640 per academic year themselves.
document_audit: A passport, national ID or travel document must be valid, and Sciences Po requires the degree itself at administrative registration (a copy can wait until end of September, but a missing degree revokes the admission offer)
Refugee applicants need the UNHCR registration card, not an asylum-seeker letter, and Sciences Po's separate fee-waiver rules for refugee status ask for an official document showing the validity date
Recommendation letters must arrive from institutional email addresses, so confirm each referee's sending address in advance rather than after submission
Language proof must sit inside the application by the deadline, and once you submit, no further document is accepted unless the Admissions office requests it
If you hold a high school diploma taught in English, keep the certificate proving the medium of instruction to claim the language-test exemption
alerts: There is no second attempt: applying once and being rejected closes this programme to you permanently, so only apply when your file is genuinely complete
The scholarship deadline overrides your programme deadline, so if Sciences Po publishes a Mastercard deadline it replaces the 21 February 2027 general closing date
You cannot defer: an offer is valid only for the academic year it is issued, and deferring your Sciences Po admission by one year forfeits the scholarship
Eligibility, admission, interview and award are four separate gates, and clearing one does not advance you through the next
Several months can pass between a Sciences Po admission offer and the scholarship decision, so do not turn down other funding while you wait
If you are admitted to Sciences Po but not selected, you are responsible for securing alternative funding, so keep a parallel Eiffel or Emile Boutmy application alive
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create one account on the Sciences Po application portal, request the fee waiver and apply to a two-year Master's in the same submission, upload every document as PDF, pay nothing if the waiver is granted, then wait for admissibility, admission, a shortlist email and a roughly 25-minute Zoom interview before any award decision.
